description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:362-376

  /// Per-aggregate count limits on roles, members, channels, and
  /// categories per Space are applied by `handle_space_set` *before*
  /// it calls this method (bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.8). The handler queries
  /// the backend's [`ChatBackend::limits`] once per request,
  /// fetches the current Space, and rejects the whole update target
  /// with an `overQuota` SetError ... This means an
  /// `apply_space_patch` call that originates from
  /// `handle_space_set` will not contain `Add*` ops that push the
  /// Space over cap. Backends called directly (bypassing the
  /// handler) MAY enforce caps a second time for defense in depth;
  /// the reference `MemoryBackend` does not.

The kit splits cap enforcement between the handler and the
backend in a way that contradicts the workspace's settled
'backend canonical for permission enforcement' policy (lib.rs:29-52,
workspace AGENTS.md 'Caller identity (foundation seam)'):

  'Backends are canonical for permission enforcement.' Handlers do
  no permission checking. Defense-in-depth handler-side pre-checks
  are allowed but the backend MUST re-verify atomically with the
  mutation. A handler that 'trusts' a handler-side check and skips
  the backend re-check is a bug.

The aggregate-count caps are exactly this kind of enforcement.
Putting the check in handle_space_set and not in the backend's
apply_space_patch means:

1. A consumer who calls apply_space_patch directly — e.g. an
   admin tool that bypasses the JMAP wire layer and operates on
   the backend directly, a federation receiver that turns a peer
   payload into ops without going through the handler, an
   internal batch importer that seeds 10k members at once — gets
   ZERO cap enforcement. The reference MemoryBackend documents
   this gap and doesn't enforce.

2. The handler-side check is non-atomic with the mutation. A
   second concurrent /set request can race past the count check
   and both commit. Even spec-compliant backends are exposed.

3. The doc tells consumers their backend 'MAY enforce caps a
   second time for defense in depth' — but every multi-tenant
   production backend that takes caps seriously will have to
   write the same boilerplate. The kit owns the cap policy
   (ChatLimits + the limits() hook) but devolves the enforcement
   to a 'MAY' on every implementor.

4. The cap-enforcement split is asymmetric vs the rest of the
   trait's policy hooks: protect_last_admin enforcement is
   backend-canonical (atomic inside apply_space_patch).
   manage_space gate on apply_space_metadata_patch is
   backend-canonical. Only caps live half-in-handler.

Fix: move cap enforcement to backend-canonical:

- Drop the handler-side cap check in handle_space_set OR keep it
  as a non-load-bearing pre-flight (defense-in-depth, as the
  workspace policy permits).
- Update the apply_space_patch trait doc to require backends to
  apply caps atomically per-op, querying self.limits() inside
  the same critical section as the mutation.
- Update MemoryBackend to enforce caps inside apply_space_patch_impl.

This is the same shape-correction we'd apply to permission gates
generally; the cap finding generalises it.
title: API contract: apply_space_patch cap-check split with handler causes admin-tool bypass
